capabilities: Roll dice with Tag and Tally resolution mechanics (advantage, disadvantage, tag bonuses, qualifiers)
Search and browse the bundled Tag and Tally rulebook from a sidebar
Generate NPCs, creatures, and scenes from editable sentence-generator notes
Draw results from random tables and card decks for prep and improv
Chat with a local AI model for prep, rules lookup, and inline summaries or evaluations
disambiguation: Not a note-tagging tool; Tag and Tally is the name of the rules-light RPG system the plugin supports.
extras: The AI assistant is off by default, requires the user to run their own local model server, and sends no requests to remote services; game content lives as editable vault notes and a starter set is installed via the command palette without overwriting edited files.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in tools for running tabletop RPG sessions, such as dice resolution, rule lookup, or improvisation generators.

relations.evidence: Install a local OpenAI-compatible model server such as LM Studio

requires.name: local OpenAI-compatible model server (e.g. LM Studio)

summary: Tabletop RPG toolkit that runs Tag and Tally sessions in a vault with dice resolution, a searchable rulebook, NPC generation, random tables, and card decks.
